references.text: The Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands thoroughly, in accordance with the tradition of the elders. This is the background for the Pharisee's expectation of ritual washing before a meal, which the Pharisee in Luke 11:38 reacted to ([ref:Mark 7:3-4|Mark 7:3-4]).

The Pharisees and scribes ask Jesus why his disciples break the tradition of the elders by not washing their hands before eating. The same theme as in Luke 11:38, where the Pharisee is surprised that Jesus did not wash before the meal ([ref:Matt 15:1-2|Matt 15:1-2]).

The Pharisees and scribes ask Jesus directly why his disciples do not follow the tradition of the elders but eat with unwashed hands. This expresses the same attitude shown by the Pharisee in Luke 11:38 ([ref:Mark 7:5|Mark 7:5]).

Jesus' response to the Pharisee's reaction in verse 38: He rebukes the Pharisees for cleaning the outside of the cup and dish while the inside is full of greed and wickedness. He exposes the hypocrisy of focusing on external ritual purity ([ref:Luk 11:39-41|Luke 11:39-41]).

Jesus pronounces woe upon the Pharisees who clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside are full of greed and self-indulgence. A parallel to Jesus' criticism of external purity practices in Luke 11:38-39 ([ref:Matt 23:25-26|Matt 23:25-26]).

Another episode where Jesus eats at a Pharisee's house, and the Pharisee reacts to Jesus' behavior—this time that he allowed a sinful woman to touch him. It shows a pattern where Pharisees invite Jesus in order to observe and criticize him ([ref:Luk 7:36-39|Luke 7:36-39]).

Once again, Jesus enters the house of a leading Pharisee to eat, and they watched him closely. It illustrates the recurring pattern of Pharisees monitoring Jesus during meals ([ref:Luk 14:1|Luke 14:1]).
The Old Testament command to rinse vessels in water is part of the background for the ritual washing rules that the Pharisees in Luke 11:38 based their tradition on ([ref:3 Mos 15:11|Lev 15:11]).
